## Load Library
```{r}
### Load Libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(phyloseq)
library(data.table)
library(purrr)
library(Biostrings)
library(stringr)
library(readr)
library(janitor)
library(ggplot2)
library(vegan)
library(randomForest)
library(caret)
```


## Read the Phyloseq Object
```{r}
ps_asv <- readRDS("ps_genus.rds")
```

## Read the master_metadata file
```{r}
metdat <- read.csv("master_metadata.csv", row.names = 1 )
```


## Extract the tables
```{r}
otu <- as.data.frame(otu_table(ps_asv))
```

```{r}
tax <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps_asv))
```


## Recreate the ps_otu object

```{r}
OTU <- otu_table(as.matrix(otu), taxa_are_rows = T)
TAX <- tax_table(as.matrix(tax))

ps_asv <- phyloseq(OTU, TAX, metdat)
```

```{r}
if (!taxa_are_rows(ps_asv)) otu <- t(otu)
```

```{r}
metdat$sample <- rownames(metdat)
```


### Scaling
```{r}
nonzero_per_sample <- colSums(otu > 20)
sort(nonzero_per_sample)[1:80]   # lowest 50 — the culprits will be at the top
```


```{r}
# Which samples specifically?
problem_samples <- names(nonzero_per_sample[nonzero_per_sample <= 1])
problem_samples

# Check metadata — study, bodysite, sequencing depth, etc.
metdat %>% filter(rownames(metdat) %in% problem_samples)

# Check raw total read count for these samples (low depth explains near-empty easily)
colSums(otu)[problem_samples]
```


```{r}
otu_filtered <- otu[, nonzero_per_sample > 1]

# Confirm how many samples got dropped
ncol(otu) - ncol(otu_filtered)
```

```{}
# RIGHT - normalize inside each fold, using only that fold's train data
folds <- createFolds(y, k = 5)
for (fold in folds) {
  train_data <- otu[, -fold]
  test_data  <- otu[, fold]
  
  # fit normalization params on train only
  css_params <- fit_css(train_data)
  train_norm <- apply_css(train_data, css_params)
  test_norm  <- apply_css(test_data, css_params)  # apply train-derived params to test
}
```

-----------Trouble Shooting----------------------------------------

```{}
s <- studies[1]  # test with just the first study

train_samples <- metdat$sample[metdat$study != s]
test_samples  <- metdat$sample[metdat$study == s]

n_bodysites_test <- n_distinct(metdat$bodysite_standard[metdat$sample %in% test_samples])
n_bodysites_test    # if this is 0, guard clause #1 is firing

train_clr <- otu_clr[, colnames(otu_clr) %in% train_samples, drop = FALSE]
test_clr  <- otu_clr[, colnames(otu_clr) %in% test_samples, drop = FALSE]

ncol(train_clr)    # if 0, guard clause #2 is firing
ncol(test_clr)     # if 0, guard clause #2 is firing
```


```{r}
head(colnames(otu_clr))
head(metdat$sample)

# Do they actually overlap at all?
sum(colnames(otu_clr) %in% metdat$sample)
length(colnames(otu_clr))
```









-------------
```{r}
set.seed(916)

for (s in studies) {
  train_samples <- metdat_filtered$sample[metdat_filtered$study != s]
  test_samples  <- metdat_filtered$sample[metdat_filtered$study == s]
  
  # Skip studies with no bodysite variety to evaluate against
  n_bodysites_test <- n_distinct(metdat_filtered$bodysite_standard[metdat_filtered$sample %in% test_samples])
  if (n_bodysites_test < 1) next
  
  train_clr <- otu_clr[, colnames(otu_clr) %in% train_samples, drop = FALSE]
  test_clr  <- otu_clr[, colnames(otu_clr) %in% test_samples, drop = FALSE]
  
  # Skip if either split ended up empty (e.g., sample ID mismatch)
  if (ncol(train_clr) == 0 || ncol(test_clr) == 0) next
  
  train_labels <- metdat_filtered$bodysite_standard[match(colnames(train_clr), metdat_filtered$sample)]
  test_labels  <- metdat_filtered$bodysite_standard[match(colnames(test_clr), metdat_filtered$sample)]
  
  rf_model <- randomForest(x = t(train_clr), y = as.factor(train_labels), ntree = 500)
  preds <- predict(rf_model, t(test_clr))
  
  loso_results[[s]] <- data.frame(
    study = s,
    sample = colnames(test_clr),
    true_bodysite = test_labels,
    predicted_bodysite = preds
  )
}

loso_all <- bind_rows(loso_results)

```

```{r}
glimpse(loso_all)
```

```{r}
loso_all$true_bodysite <- as.factor(loso_all$true_bodysite)
```


```{r}
confusionMatrix(loso_all$predicted_bodysite, loso_all$true_bodysite)

# Per-study accuracy breakdown
loso_all %>%
  group_by(study) %>%
  summarise(accuracy = mean(predicted_bodysite == true_bodysite)) %>%
  arrange(accuracy)
```
